scope: Theorem 6.1 (Projection-game repetition) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be a finite bipartite projection game, with an arbitrary probability distribution on its constraint occurrences. Question sets and answer alphabets may be arbitrary finite sets, and parallel constraint occurrences are allowed. The game G⊗n samples n independent occurrences, sends each prover its tuple of questions, and accepts if all n projection constraints hold. For every integer n ≥ 1 and every 0 < g < 1, val(G) ≤ 1 − g =⇒ val(G⊗n ) ≤ (1 − g2 /16)n . (6.1) The bound is independent of the question-set and alphabet sizes.
